extracted.intended_audience: biographers, students of literary biography, and literary critics
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles and standards for composing and judging literary biography (what to include, how candid to be, sources and style). Emphasises the biographer's obligations to truth, method, and the public while illustrating with Boswell and contemporaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between duty to subject and public expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: The biographer is 'placed between a Scylla and Charybdis, between what is due to the subject, and what is expected by the public.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw a careful line: omit too much and the likeness is imperfect; gratify inquisitiveness and risk offending. The critic must weigh private propriety against the readers' interest in knowing matters that illuminate character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of a subject's peculiarities and blemishes
rubrics_metrics.description: In writing a man's life 'the man's peculiarities should be mentioned because they mark his character.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peculiarities and 'slight blemishes' are integral to a truthful portrait. Examples: Boswell's deliberate inclusion of Johnson's colloquial traits; excluding such traits (or disguising affairs like Nelson's) is disingenuous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candour about private details after a subject's death
rubrics_metrics.description: After the man is dead, it is historical to expose defects or private matters: 'Why, no, sir,... after the man is dead, for then it is done historically.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private letters and confidences may legitimately be published if they are historically relevant. The biographer should not shy from sensitive material on the sole ground that it offends respectability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veracity (truthfulness) as the primary obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Biography is assigned to the department of oratory and 'the field for the display of every other feeling then veracity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Truth should govern selection and presentation. Emotional tone or rhetorical flourish must not supersede factual fidelity; withholding facts in the name of decorum misconceives the biographer's duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of first-hand and 'authentick' materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever first-hand information could be had, Boswell 'was constantly on the track' to secure 'authentick' material gathered over years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek letters, conversations, diaries, eyewitness accounts, and other primary sources; persist despite rebuffs. Such materials underpin a credible and vivid life-writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding excessive dignity/respectability that sanitizes the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Dignity and respectability have 'ruined alike the historian and the biographer' by excluding everything beneath the perceived dignity of the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not confine the narrative to courts, battles, or high offices alone; include ordinary and undignified details that reveal manners and real life (Hogarth and Fielding are cited as better guides to manners than court gazettes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Method: integrate letters, conversations, and anecdote into the scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: The inclusion of the letters and of private details was 'an integral part of his scheme' for Boswell's Life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize and interweave correspondence, journals, and candid anecdotes to present character and colloquial talents; these materials can transform perception of the subject (e.g., enhancing Johnson's portrait).

rubrics_metrics.name: Candid treatment may rightly offend critics but fulfills biographer's duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism that certain passages should have been omitted 'is to seriously misconceive the province and duty of the biographer.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate charges of indiscretion or lack of delicacy; prioritize truthful and intelligible reporting over pleasing reviewers or preserving reputations when material is relevant to understanding the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style preference: make biography familiar rather than merely heroic
rubrics_metrics.description: 'I would have History familiar rather than heroic'—biography should convey everyday manners and human detail, not only stately grandeur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a manner that shows character by ordinary actions and speech as much as by public deeds; familiarity can give readers a better sense of an age and person than grand, court-centered narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographer as orator: clarity and intelligibility of presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Latin critics assigned history and biography 'to the department of oratory'—the biographer must present material clearly and intelligibly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange facts and testimony so the portrait is coherent and rhetorically effective without sacrificing accuracy; rhetorical skill should illuminate veracity rather than obscure it.
